candidates.decision_relevance: Would make the repeatedly cited breadth changes auditable and distinguish market-wide participation changes from shifts in proxy membership; current captures use different membership hashes and some are post-cutoff.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily outputs dated 2026-10-02 through 2026-10-05 report proxy breadth with changing point-in-time membership; weekly reviews also note missing breadth methodology and history.
candidates.metric_name: Timestamped constituent-level breadth observations with stable universe or explicit membership snapshots
candidates.missing_history_problem: Comparable historical membership and constituent observations are not supplied, so breadth persistence, constituent-level changes, and its ordering relative to price weakness cannot be assessed.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would show whether settled BTC and ETH flow support persisted, reversed, or diverged across sessions, rather than relying on isolated mixed daily rows or weekly totals whose timing relative to deterioration is unclear.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily outputs repeatedly cite one settled session (for example, October 1 or October 2) and state that it does not establish a trend; weekly reviews identify missing settled-flow sequence and timing.
candidates.metric_name: Per-session settled BTC and ETH ETF net flows with settlement dates and retrieval/availability timestamps
candidates.missing_history_problem: The supplied records provide isolated settled observations or aggregate weekly descriptions, not a dated multi-session sequence aligned to the price and breadth observations.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would resolve whether reported short-horizon weakness preceded or followed rebounds and would permit consistent reconstruction of BTC and ETH paths at decision cutoffs; multiple analyses report unavailable or shortened nominal API windows and timestamp misalignment.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily outputs report missing 1-hour anchors, zero-span or shortened nominal windows, and post-cutoff observations; weekly reviews identify absent raw paths and event-time alignment.
candidates.metric_name: Timestamped hourly BTC and ETH price observations with actual interval endpoints and cutoff-time availability
candidates.missing_history_problem: The records provide inconsistent actual spans and endpoint summaries rather than a continuous, cutoff-auditable price sequence, leaving path ordering and short-window calculations uncertain.
